gaps.sentence: ___ influenza, or flu, is highly contagious.
gaps.explanation: Most disease names take no article: influenza, flu, malaria (compare: the flu is also heard informally).

gaps.sentence: He behaves as if he were ___ owner of the company.
gaps.explanation: 'The owner' — there is one owner, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ problem is that people don't recycle enough.
gaps.explanation: The problem (the one we are discussing); people in general takes no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
gaps.explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).

gaps.sentence: She was wearing ___ old denim jacket that I loved at first sight.
gaps.explanation: 'An old…' — 'old' starts with a vowel sound.
Both 'happiness' and 'money' are general here, so no article for either gap.

gaps.sentence: His wife goes to ___ prison every Sunday to visit him.
gaps.explanation: Here 'the prison' is the building she visits, not the institution of imprisonment.

gaps.sentence: He gave me ___ useful advice about the paperwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — never 'an advice'. Use 'a piece of advice' for one item.
